transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Ever since that car drove into the crowd, even little sounds make me feel like I’m back there and I jump out of my chair or drop things. I just can't seem to shake this feeling of being constantly on edge.
I'm so sorry you had to go through that. How long ago did this incident with the car happen, and how long have you been feeling this way?
The accident at the street fair happened about a week ago. All of these feelings started immediately in the days right after it, and it's been going on like this every day since.
Have you found yourself actively trying to avoid thoughts, feelings, or places—like the street fair area—that remind you of the accident?

Yes, I've been actively avoiding all of it. I'm turning down rides past downtown, skipping Mass, and avoiding the senior center because just thinking about busy streets or crowds makes my chest tighten up. I try to push those thoughts and feelings out of my mind as fast as I can.
Are you also experiencing upsetting dreams about the accident, or sudden, vivid memories where it feels like it is happening all over again?

Yes, during the day it’s like a film stuck on repeat where I suddenly see that car jump the curb and my friend getting hit, and it feels so real I have to grab the counter to steady myself. Then at night, if I finally do nod off, I jerk awake with my heart racing from those exact same images.
Immediately after the accident, or even now, did you feel 'dazed,' emotionally numb, or as if you were detached from your surroundings?

I didn't really feel numb or detached from myself, but I was extremely terrified, overwhelmed, and confused by how chaotic the whole scene was. Now, I'm mostly just feeling incredibly jumpy and on edge all the time.
Have you noticed any changes in your mood or thoughts since the accident, such as blaming yourself, feeling constant guilt, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?

I don't really blame myself or feel guilty about the accident itself, but my mood has changed and I've completely stopped doing things I used to enjoy, like gardening, church, and my art classes. I feel too overwhelmed to leave the house, and I've been incredibly irritable, even snapping and barking at a kind neighbor who just brought me some soup.
Over this past week, have you noticed these feelings starting to ease up or fade at all, or have they remained just as intense as they were right after the accident?

They haven't eased up at all, to be honest. If anything, they've stayed just as intense, and some days feel even worse than right after it happened. It still feels like that car jumped the curb just yesterday.

The clinical picture is highly characteristic of F43.1 (Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder). While a formal diagnosis of PTSD often requires symptoms to persist for a longer duration (typically 1 month), F43.1 is the most accurate clinical fit for the ongoing presentation, and F43.0 is now excluded due to the prolonged duration.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient experienced a highly traumatic event one week ago when a car drove into a crowd and struck her friend. She presents with a constellation of symptoms characteristic of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1), including intrusive flashbacks and nightmares, active avoidance of trauma-related reminders (places, thoughts, and activities), persistent hyperarousal (exaggerated startle response, constant tension, and irritability), and negative alterations in mood and behavior (loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities and social withdrawal). These symptoms began immediately after the event, have remained intense, and are causing significant functional impairment.
